draft.title: Special interest groups
card: A special interest group is an organised group of people who share a cause. It tries to influence what businesses do, but it does not own or run them.
pushes businesses to protect the environment, for example by cutting waste or pollution.
represents businesses in an industry. It may lobby governments and offer members advice and support.
represents employees. It may push for better pay, safer conditions and fair treatment at work.
draft.remember: Special interest groups try to influence a business from outside, each for its own cause.

a.q: A group of workers at a bakery chain joins an organisation that pushes the chain for safer working conditions. What type of group is it?
a.why: A union represents employees and pushes for better conditions at work. A business association speaks for businesses, not their workers, so it does not fit.
a.clue: Who does the group speak for: owners or employees?

b.q: Priya runs a small cabinet-making business in Geelong. A group she does not belong to campaigns for her to stop using timber from old forests. What best describes this group's influence?
opts: It can pressure her, but it cannot run her business
It can direct her business, as it speaks for the industry
It can pressure her, as it represents her employees
It can pressure her only if she is a member of it
b.why: An environmental group tries to influence a business from outside through pressure and campaigns, but it does not own or run it. The tempting option is that it directs her business, but a special interest group has no control over decisions.
b.clue: Think about what the group wants, and whether it has any say in running the business.

b.best: It can pressure her, but it cannot run her business
